text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein says after talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba that the region "is living through a very dangerous period and Jordan committed to peace".
- King Hussein says two options face the region: progress or catastrophe; Netanyahu says ready to discuss settlments issue on the negotiating table.
- Parliament Speaker Saed Srour says will continue contacts with opposition parties to remove hurdles to their participation in the coming parliamentary elections due to be held next November.
- A draft law on the independence of the judiciary to be submitted next week to the cabinet.
- King Hussein briefs Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and U.S. President Bill Clinton on results of the Aqaba meeting with Netanyahu.
- Brotherhood values king's wish to revoke election boycott, says it is pending government talks.
